issues.detail: The Greek 'ιδου εση σιωπων' (behold, you shall be silent) is rendered as 'ngươi sẽ làm thinh' (you will be silent). The Greek uses the future passive/middle construction of 'sigma' (σιωπῶ), but more importantly, it is a command/prophecy of silence. However, the Vietnamese 'làm thinh' can imply a voluntary act of keeping quiet, whereas the Greek implies a state of being silenced or rendered mute by God.

The Greek 'μη δυναμενος λαλησαι' (not being able to speak) is rendered as 'không nói được' (cannot speak). While accurate in meaning, the Vietnamese structure makes it sound like a secondary description of the silence rather than the specific inability to speak that is the grammatical condition in the Greek.
